symptom: `call microflow M.ACT_Close as close` in a workflow gives a bare "mismatched input 'close' expecting {IDENTIFIER, QUOTED_IDENTIFIER}"; `returns Boolean as $Ok` after `exposed as workflow action 'A' in 'C'` gives "mismatched input 'returns' expecting BEGIN" (or STRING_LITERAL inside the clause), read as 'an exposed microflow cannot return a value'
cause: The keyword hint only matched the fixed 41-word hintedKeywordSet, so any other lexer keyword in a name slot got no hint; the routine header grammar fixes `microflowReturnType` before `microflowOptions` and nothing explained the order
insight: A keyword-in-name-slot test needs no keyword list: an identifier-shaped offending token with QUOTED_IDENTIFIER in the RAW expecting set (read before simplifyExpecting truncates it) can only be a lexer keyword, and quoting is exactly what that set allows. Key on QUOTED_IDENTIFIER, not IDENTIFIER — the statement-start set also lists IDENTIFIER and `end` there would be told to quote itself. For a header-order hint the parser context is the discriminator, not the message: walk GetParserRuleContext() up to Create{Microflow,Nanoflow,Rule}StatementContext, but stop at MicroflowBodyContext AND treat a create context that already has a body child as past the header — a stray `returns` before END reports from the create context too (the body-control test caught that).
